newsitem.title: UK: Britain charts path for global free trade by 2020.
newsitem.headline: Britain charts path for global free trade by 2020.

text.p: Britain's Conservative government on Monday stressed its determination to achieve a complete dismantling of trade barriers across the world by the year 2020.

With a ministerial conference of the World Trade Organisation scheduled for next month in Singapore, Britain published a policy White Paper calling for a new round of global trade talks to begin by the end of this decade.

Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang told a news conference Britain had already pressed the European Union into setting up a genuine single market covering the bloc, the largest free trade area in the world.
"We now see an opportunity for spreading the open markets message on a truly global scale," he said.

Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said that since the end of the Cold War, the growth in democratic institutions in the world had gone hand in hand with an increasing reliance on market mechanisms in economic policy.
"If we can achieve free trade throughout the world, this will be a massive contribution to confidence and stability at the international level."

He said Britain's target of 2020 for complete free trade was backed by a number of other countries. He believed it was "neither so far away as to excite disinterest, nor so near as to be unrealistic".
But Rifkind warned that even EU countries showed dangerous protectionist attitudes when it came to their agricultural industries.
He described as "quite pathetic" efforts by some EU states to keep farm produce such as strawberry jam and cabbages from Eastern European countries out of the bloc's market.
"As these countries become members of the European Union, they will have completely open access, and the sooner we get used to that, the better," Rifkind said.
